_comment: The tests that carry seclume's security claims, by the CI job that runs them.
security_gate.py reads the job's surefire reports and gives each one a status:
PASS (run, nothing skipped, nothing failed), FAIL (failed, or not run at all),
SKIPPED (every case skipped), INCONCLUSIVE (some cases skipped) or NOT APPLICABLE
(this platform is not one the test is for). Only PASS and NOT APPLICABLE let a
build through: a skipped security test is never a passed one. Where a test may
skip cases on a platform for a reason, 'skips' names the platform and the reason,
and the status is PASS with the reason shown - never silently.

core.property: no production code puts a secret on the heap without a marked reason
no exception message carries a secret
a secret scope is zero after close, read back from its memory
a scope wiped from another thread is wiped completely
errors, stack overflows and concurrent closes leave no scope open
native memory refused at allocation leaves nothing open, and what was made stays whole and is wiped
a failing provider or reader leaves its buffer wiped
secret pages are locked against swap
locking and dump exclusion hold under limits and concurrency

skips.windows-x64: the dump-exclusion cases read /proc/self/smaps, which only Linux has

core.property: secret pages are excluded from core dumps (MADV_DONTDUMP, WerRegisterExcludedMemoryBlock)
an untrusted, mismatched or wrongly used certificate is refused
host names match as RFC 6125 says, wildcards and public suffixes included
a server below the configured TLS version is refused
a TLS 1.2 server with an untrusted certificate is refused
trust settings cannot be weakened by accident
no fuzzed server flight connects without authentication
the TLS 1.3 key schedule matches RFC 8448
AES-GCM, AES-GCM-SIV, HMAC, HKDF, PBKDF2 and ECDH pass Wycheproof
AES-GCM-SIV reveals only equality under a repeated nonce, and an altered value leaves no plaintext
field encryption's format is pinned against an independent implementation; altered, copied and foreign values are refused
over thousands of random rings, columns and values, what is encrypted decrypts to itself and to nothing else
a data key unwrapped by Vault transit reaches native memory only, and every refusal is said
SCRAM channel binding is computed from the server's certificate
a secret manager's answer is read in place, nothing outside the value copied
the heap-dump search finds a secret that is there (negative control) and none that is not
redaction searches for the application's secrets without a heap copy of them
a Flight Recorder recording is redacted and still reads
heapcheck finds a secret in a running JVM and reports none it does not hold

skips.windows-x64: --in-target reads through /proc/<pid>/root, which only Linux has

core.property: heapcheck refuses a secret as an argument and fails rather than reporting a heap it could not read

postgresql.property: a connection that fails leaves no secret in its buffers
received bytes are wiped once read
the server holds only ciphertext; a heap dump after a read holds neither the value nor the key
